23rd July – 3rd August 
Import premiums flat as domestic production rises 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Import premiums for copper cathode over the past fortnight remained largely within the same range as two 
weeks ago - between $70 and $80.  Import activity remains quiet as demand is still weak and the SHFE/LME 
arbitrage was negative, disfavouring cathode imports.  We heard that traders interested in importing could 
potentially have incurred a cathode import loss as high as $300/t when the SHFE/LME arbitrage was at its 
most negative (-$195/t on 26th July).  Since then, the SHFE/LME price differential narrowed, reaching -$5/t on 
1st August, which suggests that cathode availability is beginning to weaken.  Inventories in SHFE and bonded 
warehouses changed very little; with levels at the end of 3rd August at 164,111t and 550,000t, respectively.

The SHFE price declined over the past fortnight, however, the physical market held up better than the SHFE 
cash-month and 3M prices, which caused a backwardation between the physical and cash-month prices.  In the 
week beginning 23rd July, the backwardation averaged RMB270/t, the highest it has been for a month.   It 
seems that demand for copper on the physical market has risen slightly and has been met by rising domestic 
refined copper production rather than by destocking at SHFE or bonded warehouses.  As reported in the 
previous edition, refined production grew by 7% y-o-y in June and we suspect that it maintained a strong rate 
of growth through July.  In the week beginning 30th July, the physical/cash-month price backwardation 
narrowed to an average of RMB127/t, showing that there is still an elevated requirement for immediate cathode 
delivery, which we again attribute to a slight recovery in demand.   
Overall, sentiment is still gloomy because of the ongoing euro debt crisis.  This has continued to subdue 
demand as the supply chain orders cautiously.  We also note that any improvement in underlying demand for 
copper products will not be felt immediately in the market for refined copper cathode as stock levels through 
the supply chain are very high.  The softness in demand seen in the year so far is also the result of weaker than 
expected infrastructure investment.   This is particularly evident in the power utility industry. 
Power industry performance in H1 
The government has said that it wishes to shift toward an increasingly consumption-driven economy rather 
than investment and export-led economic growth.  The Chinese copper industry is however, heavily supported 
by investment, particularly from infrastructure development.  The largest sector of which is the development of 
the power grid. 
The China Electricity Council recently reported details of investments made in the power industry in the first 
half of the year.  Fixed asset investment in the power grid totalled RMB139.3B, up by 8.0% y-o-y in H1.  Fixed 
asset investment in power generation was RMB146.1B in H1, representing a decrease of 2.7% y-o-y. 
Breaking down the power grid investment for H1 reveals that RMB23.2B was used in power grids for rural 
areas.  20% of the money for this investment was supplied from government revenue and 80% from the 
Agricultural Development Bank.  The State Grid invested RMB1.69B, which represents only 3.7% of its 
targeted investment of RMB45.8B in rural power networks in the whole of 2012.  In order for the power utility 
operator to meet the full year targeted investment it would have to rapidly accelerate grid development 
expenditure in H2.  This may however be difficult to achieve given the current tight credit availability, which 
impacts the State Grid’s suppliers.  It is also important to note that the State Grid did not fully invest its 
RMB37.8B allocation for rural grid projects in 2011, which means that in context of the wider 12th Five Year 
Plan (2011-2015), the State Grid may well be significantly under-performing on investment terms by year-end.  
The 12th Five Year Plan specified that the State Grid will invest RMB400B and Southern Grid would invest 
RMB110B. 
Fixed asset investment in power generation is not as copper intensive compared to that of power grid projects.  
Even so, the vastness of the investment package, RMB146.1B in H1, means that the sector still represents a 
significant auxiliary market for copper products.  The China Electricity Council earlier reported that planned 
investment in the power generation sector amounts to RMB350B, which means that spending should accelerate 
slightly in H2 of this year.  New installed power generation capacity above 6000kW totalled 1047GW, up by 
8.7% y-o-y in H1 2012.  Investment in hydropower grew at the fastest rate of all the power sources, rising 46%

Prices falls while waiting for Eurozone and US 
intervention 
 
After the SHFE 3-month price edged up to RMB56,320/t on Thursday 20th July on speculation of a new 
Chinese growth stimulus package following weak GDP data for Q2, the momentum of the SHFE and LME 3-
month price reversed as focus shifted once again to the Eurozone.  Negative sentiment reappeared on fears that 
Spain might require a more comprehensive bail-out after Spanish bond yields reached a new high of 7.56% on 
Monday 23rd July, followed by news one day later that borrowing costs had risen to a euro-high of 7.5%.  In 
addition to this, Moody’s changed its outlook rating to negative for Germany, the Netherlands and 
Luxembourg.  In response, SHFE 3-month prices fell steadily to reach RMB53,630/t, a one month low on 25th 
July. 
An announcement made by the chief of the European Central Bank (ECB) on Thursday 26th July, promising to 
take whatever action necessary to avoid the break-up of the Eurozone, restored some fragile confidence in 
financial and metal markets.  This prompted a rise in 3-month copper prices at the SHFE, reaching 
RMB54,770/t at close of trading on Friday 27th July.  Copper prices traded sideways for the first half of the past 
week, peaking at RMB55,050/t on Tuesday 31st July as market participants awaited the outcome from separate 
meetings involving the ECB, and Federal Reserve in Europe and the US.  The results, however, failed to assure 
markets as the 3-month SHFE price declined again, reaching RMB54,100/t on Friday 3rd August. 
The SHFE/LME price arbitrage remained negative throughout the past two weeks, discouraging Chinese 
cathode imports.  The price differential did temporarily narrow to just US$5/t on Thursday 2nd August due to 
LME prices responding more sensitively to the latest news of European and US policymakers’ failure to offer 
reassuring plans and intervention to counteract weak economic growth.  One day later, the price differential 
expanded once again due to US jobs data released late in the day, which strengthened the US dollar, resulting 
in LME 3-month prices falling to US$7,445/t.  We expect SHFE prices will recover slightly in the forthcoming 
weeks to closer match those in the LME as Chinese investment and stimuli improve demand.

SHFE copper cathode inventories fell for the first time in one month during the week ending 27th July, 
declining by 4,463t.  The destocking was short-lived though, as SHFE stocks rose by 7,601t in the following 
week, closing on Friday 3rd August at 164,111t.
